purpose: Candidate peer-reviewed and prepublication sources distinguishing formal relational reasoning, cognitive restructuring, cognitive reappraisal and evidence-sensitive reframing.

records.citation: May, R. J., Tyndall, I., McTiernan, A., Roderique-Davies, G., & McLoughlin, S. (2022). The impact of the SMART program on cognitive and academic skills: A systematic review and meta-analysis. British Journal of Educational Technology, 53, 1244-1261.
records.population: five school-based studies with 195 analysed participants
key_findings: moderate pooled effect on nonverbal IQ, g = 0.57
insufficient evidence for other cognitive or academic domains
all included primary-outcome studies were rated high risk of bias
limitations: does not validate the IQ Mindware Reasoning protocol

records.citation: Ciharova, M., Furukawa, T. A., Efthimiou, O., Karyotaki, E., Miguel, C., Noma, H., Cipriani, A., Riper, H., & Cuijpers, P. (2021). Cognitive restructuring, behavioral activation and cognitive-behavioral therapy in the treatment of adult depression: A network meta-analysis. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 89(6), 563-574.
key_findings: no evidence of differential effectiveness among cognitive restructuring, behavioural activation and combined CBT
all three interventions outperformed care as usual and waiting list
limitations: does not validate a generic digital reasoning app

records.citation: Papola, D., et al. (2024). Psychotherapies for generalized anxiety disorder in adults: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials. JAMA Psychiatry, 81(3), 250-259.
records.population: 65 randomized trials with 5048 adults with generalized anxiety disorder
key_findings: CBT had the strongest and most durable evidence
pure cognitive restructuring was not decisively active when isolated
limitations: interventions varied in content and delivery

records.citation: Furukawa, Y., et al. (2024). Components and delivery formats of cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic insomnia in adults: A systematic review and component network meta-analysis. JAMA Psychiatry, 81(4), 357-365.
records.population: 241 trials with 31452 adults with chronic insomnia
key_findings: cognitive restructuring was associated with higher remission
cognitive restructuring was associated with improved subjective sleep quality
limitations: component effects may interact with other treatment elements
does not establish efficacy of a generic reasoning task

records.citation: Braun, J. D., Strunk, D. R., Sasso, K. E., & Cooper, A. A. (2015). Therapist use of Socratic questioning predicts session-to-session symptom change in cognitive therapy for depression. Behaviour Research and Therapy, 70, 32-37.
records.population: 55 adults receiving cognitive therapy for depression
key_findings: therapist Socratic questioning predicted next-session symptom change

records.citation: Vittorio, L. N., Murphy, S. T., Braun, J. D., & Strunk, D. R. (2022). Using Socratic questioning to promote cognitive change and achieve depressive symptom reduction: Evidence of cognitive change as a mediator. Behaviour Research and Therapy, 150, 104035.
records.population: 123 clients receiving cognitive therapy for depression
key_findings: cognitive change mediated the relationship between Socratic questioning and subsequent depressive-symptom change
limitations: process evidence rather than randomized dismantling

records.citation: McManus, F., Van Doorn, K., & Yiend, J. (2012). Examining the effects of thought records and behavioral experiments in instigating belief change. Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry, 43(1), 540-547.
key_findings: both thought records and behavioural experiments produced beneficial changes relative to control across belief, anxiety, behaviour and symptom-related measures

records.citation: Yovel, I., Mor, N., & Shakarov, H. (2014). Examination of the core cognitive components of cognitive behavioral therapy and acceptance and commitment therapy: An analogue investigation. Behavior Therapy, 45(4), 482-494.
key_findings: brief cognitive restructuring and defusion both reduced distress relative to a negative-thought-focused control
improvement was associated with theoretically distinct strategies
limitations: does not establish clinical or product efficacy

records.citation: Toh, W. X., Keh, J. S., Gross, J. J., & Carstensen, L. L. (2024). The role of executive function in cognitive reappraisal: A meta-analytic review. Emotion, 24(7), 1563-1581.
key_findings: small associations between reappraisal and inhibition, updating and shifting, r = .13-.19
limitations: reappraisal measures and tasks were heterogeneous
does not equate executive-function training with reappraisal training

records.citation: Zhou, J., et al. (2025). Crisp: Cognitive Restructuring of Negative Thoughts through Multi-turn Supportive Dialogues. arXiv:2504.17238.
key_findings: proposes data and models for multi-turn cognitive-restructuring dialogue
limitations: does not establish clinical efficacy or safety
model performance is not therapeutic outcome evidence

records.citation: Zhang, M., et al. (2026). The Art of Socratic Inquiry: A Framework for Proactive Template-Guided Therapeutic Conversation Generation. arXiv:2602.01598.
records.population: synthetic and/or curated therapeutic dialogue material
key_findings: proposes a structured framework for generating Socratic-style therapeutic conversations
limitations: does not establish efficacy, safety or therapist equivalence

records.citation: Rodriguez-Juan, J., et al. (2026). ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance. arXiv:2608.04524.
key_findings: proposes a framework for generating structured CBT sessions with dynamic patient resistance
limitations: synthetic plausibility is not treatment evidence
chain-of-thought generation does not establish safe clinical reasoning
